9660.explanation:

"Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it...This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

Jacob named the place Bethel, which means "House of God," because he believed that the place was the gate of heaven—a connection point between heaven and earth, where God's presence was revealed to him in a powerful way.

9706.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
9706.question_text: How did God convince Jeremiah of his divine call?
9706.explanation:
The account of Jeremiah’s confrontation by God in the deepest zone of his being is given in the form of a dialogue. He did not receive his call to the prophetic ministry in the midst of a temple filled with brilliant light or surrounded by strange heavenly creatures. “The revelation came to him not from cloven skies, or out of the midst of the thunders of the heavens.”[39] Instead of the spectacular, Jeremiah describes the objects or events of common daily experience as the starting point for his perception of the divine truth.

If Jeremiah’s experience took the form of a vision, it was a “calm meditative vision” that was not accompanied by any spectacular phenomena. It was an experience with God on life’s way. God chose him, met him, spoke to him, touched his lips, and commissioned him as a prophet. see ''jeremiah 1 to the end''

options.text: He spoke to him directly from heaven
He sent a prophet to inform him

9782.question_text: James in his Epistle urged the brethren to count their trials all joy because the testing of their faith produces
9782.explanation:
In James 1:2-3 (RSV), James writes:

"Count it all joy, my brethren, when you meet various trials, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness."

This means that trials and challenges in life serve to strengthen one's faith and endurance. By enduring difficulties with faith, believers grow in perseverance, which helps them remain firm in their commitment to God.
